summary: Hiromasa Tosaki was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy. He earned his PhD at Kyushu University and studied at Harvard under Daniel H. H. Ingalls, among others. He held posts at Chikushi Jogakuen Junior College and Kyushu University.

Hiromi Habata works in Buddhist studies and Indology, having earned a Ph.D from the University of Freiburg. Affiliations include a researcher post at the University of Munich and appointments at the International Institute for Buddhist Studies and ICPBS.
Hiromi Yoshimura is a Buddhist studies scholar who taught Shindo Kusumoto and held posts at Ryukoku University, attested in 1987 as a full-time lecturer and in 2006.
Hiromichi Kato is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Ryogon Fukuhara as a graduate student. He taught Collett Cox and served as a lecturer at Ryukoku University, attested in 1987.

Hiromitsu Ikuma specializes in Buddhist studies and completed a doctorate at Tohoku University by 2019. He has held researcher posts at Taisho University (attested 2020) and the Shingon Buzan Comprehensive Research Institute.
Hiromu Kitanishi was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Otani University, where he later served as a professor from around 1968 to 1995.

Hironobu Minami works in Buddhist studies. He was a research assistant at the Chion'in Jodo Sect Research Institute (attested 2015) and an associate professor at Kyoto Bunkyo University (attested 2026).
Hironori Tanaka works in Buddhist studies and Indology. He completed PhD studies and held a post at Bukkyo University, and is attested as a lecturer at Kyoto Bunkyo University in 2026.

Hiroo Kashiwagi is a Buddhist studies scholar who completed doctoral coursework at the University of Tokyo and taught Waso Harada. He was a professor at Matsusaka University and president of Matsusaka Women's Junior College (~1985–1991).

Hiroo Sato is a scholar of religious studies, Buddhist studies, and Japanology. He studied at Tohoku University (~1972–1982) and held positions at Morioka College (~1982–1987) and Tohoku University, where he was a professor (~2001–2019).

Hiroshi Aoyagi works in linguistics, Japanology, and religious studies. He studied at International Christian University and earned a PhD at the University of Southern California, later serving as professor at Nanzan University circa 2007.

Hiroshi Araki is a Japanology and Buddhist studies scholar who earned his degrees at Kyoto University. He taught at Aichi Prefectural University, Osaka University, and was a professor at the International Research Center for Japanese Studies (2010–2025).

Hiroshi Arami is a scholar of Sinology and Buddhist studies who is attested as a lecturer at both the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies and the International Institute for Buddhist Studies in 2026.
Hiroshi Deguchi studied at the University of Tokyo from around 1948 to 1953 and later held a post at Hokkaido University.
Hiroshi Kanaseki was a scholar of history and archaeology who studied at Kyoto University from around 1948 to 1951 and held a post at Tenri University from around 1964 to 1997.

Hiroshi Kanno specializes in Buddhist studies, Sinology, and philosophy. Educated at the University of Tokyo, he has held posts at Toho Kenkyukai, The Institute of Oriental Philosophy, Soka University, and the International Research Institute for Advanced Buddhology.

Hiroshi Kuroda is an Indology and philosophy scholar who completed doctoral coursework at Kyoto University (~1974–1976). He served as an assistant professor at Osaka Gakuin University (attested 1983–1986) and Osaka Gakuin College (attested 1988).

Hiroshi Marui is an Indology and philosophy scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo, Pune University, and under Albrecht Wezler. He held posts at the Eastern Institute, Musashino University, and the University of Tokyo.
Hiroshi Maruyama was a scholar active in Indology who served as a professor at Osaka University and led the Ayurveda Research Society, both attested in 1987.
Hiroshi Nemoto is a Tibetology and Buddhist studies scholar who completed an MA at Hiroshima University, where he has served as an associate professor (attested 2015) and professor (attested 2026).
